name: schema
description: The database schema a build module's migrations build: Flyway migrations, Liquibase changelogs or other SQL files. Its key is the module's groupId:artifactId, or the repository name for a repository without modules. It has no C4 level: which data store holds it is decided from the datasource configuration, since several schemas may share one database.

name: table
description: A table of a schema. Its key is the schema's key, ':' and the table name as the database folds it (unquoted names in lower case), qualified with a database schema when the migrations name one, such as com.acme:orders-app:orders. It has no C4 level: a table is part of a data store.

name: column
description: A column of a table. Its key is the table's key, '#' and the column name, such as com.acme:orders-app:orders#id.

name: PRIMARY_KEY
description: The subject table's primary key includes the object column.

columns.description: All the key's column names, in key order.

name.description: The constraint name, if the migrations give one.

name: UNIQUE_KEY
description: A unique key of the subject table includes the object column. A table may have several; the columns attribute tells them apart.

columns.description: All the key's column names, in key order.

name.description: The constraint name, if the migrations give one.

name: REFERENCES
description: A foreign key of the subject table references the object table. The object may be a table the schema does not create.

columns.description: The subject table's column names, in key order.

referencedColumns.description: The object table's column names, in the same order; absent when the key names none and the object's primary key is not known.

name.description: The constraint name, if the migrations give one.

name: data-type
description: The SQL type of the subject column as the migrations write it, in lower case, such as varchar(200) or bigint.

name: nullable
description: Whether the subject column accepts null.

name: position
description: The subject's place among its siblings, from 1. For a column, its place in its table.
